title: Bellagio Resort & Casino — Overview and history
body: Public edition. Public records, fact-checked reference. Bellagio is a luxury hotel and casino on the Las Vegas Strip, opened on October 15, 1998, by Steve Wynn's Mirage Resorts at a then-record cost of about 1.6 billion dollars. It is now operated by MGM Resorts International. The resort is best known for the Fountains of Bellagio, the dancing water show on its 8.5-acre lake, and for the Conservatory and Botanical Gardens. It holds roughly 3,950 guest rooms and suites and a casino floor of about 116,000 square feet.

title: Bellagio Resort & Casino — Offerings and services
body: Public edition. Public records, fact-checked reference. Bellagio Resort & Casino offers the following, as published by the organization: 1. Casino floor with slots, table games, race and sports book, and a high-limit salon. 2. Fountains of Bellagio dancing water shows (free, several times daily). 3. Conservatory and Botanical Gardens seasonal displays (free). 4. Cirque-style resident productions and headline entertainment. 5. Fine dining restaurants and lounges. 6. Bellagio Gallery of Fine Art. 7. Spa, salon, fitness center, and pool courtyards. 8. Meeting and convention space..

title: Bellagio Resort & Casino — Notable milestones and public record
body: Public edition. Public records, fact-checked reference. Milestones in the public record: 1998: Bellagio opens on the site of the demolished Dunes hotel-casino. 2000: MGM Grand acquires Mirage Resorts, bringing Bellagio into MGM. 2005: "O" by Cirque du Soleil opens in the Bellagio Theater. 2018: Fountains of Bellagio show catalog refreshed with new music. 2019: MGM sells Bellagio real estate to Blackstone in a sale-leaseback; MGM keeps operations. 2023: Bellagio celebrates 25 years on the Strip.

title: Bellagio Resort & Casino — Visiting, hours, and access
body: Public edition. Public records, fact-checked reference. Bellagio is open 24 hours; guests must be 21 or older on the casino floor. The Fountains shows and Conservatory are free and open to the public. Valet and self-parking are available; the resort sits at the corner of Las Vegas Boulevard and Flamingo Road.
